summary: This bill amends Clean Air Act section 319(b) to expand the definition of exceptional events to include prescribed fires and similar state-approved actions to mitigate wildfire risk, requires EPA to revise its regulations within 18 months to allow exclusion of affected air quality data from regulatory determinations, and mandates regional modeling for multistate events plus a public petition-tracking website.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends Clean Air Act provisions on exceptional events and wildfire mitigation actions but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It is purely regulatory in nature.
No provisions address taxes, tax credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions concerning military or defense spending or policy.

The bill amends the Clean Air Act to expand the definition of exceptional events to explicitly include 'actions to mitigate wildfire risk' (prescribed fires) and requires regulatory revisions that make it easier to exclude air quality data influenced by wildfires or prescribed burns from NAAQS determinations, area designations, and attainment findings. This reduces the regulatory impact of air quality standards in fire-prone regions and facilitates wildfire risk reduction activities, thereby limiting the stringency of environmental regulations.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
